title: Choose your platforms and grow a real audience

say: Choose your platforms, and grow a real audience.
This is the video for module one of Social Media Marketing for Business.
Social media marketing helps the right people find your business, trust it and buy from it. It starts with knowing exactly who your customer is.

say: Step one. Write one sentence about your best customer: who she is, where she lives, what she needs, and how she likes to buy. This is your target audience.

say: Step two. Pick one main platform where your customers discover businesses. Instagram suits anything visual, like fashion, beauty and food. TikTok suits products you can demonstrate. Facebook suits local services and community selling.

say: Step four. Facebook, Instagram and TikTok help people discover you, but WhatsApp is where most Nigerian small businesses close the sale. So send every enquiry there.

say: Step five. After 30 days, review using real enquiries, not likes.
Funmi, who sells small chops in Ibadan, chose Facebook as main and Instagram as support, and gets every order in one WhatsApp inbox.

panel.rule: Posting once a month on five platforms looks abandoned.

say: Your profile must answer four questions fast. What do you sell? Where? Can I trust you? How do I order?
Ada sells Ankara dresses in Abuja. Her old bio said, God's own designer, blessed, DM for enquiries. It answered none of them.

panel.heading: Ada rewrites a weak bio
left: No sizes, no area, no link
right: Ankara dresses for work and owambe

say: She switched to a Business account and rewrote it: ready-to-wear Ankara dresses for work and owambe, sizes 8 to 20, delivery across Abuja, order on WhatsApp below.
She added her wa.me link and Highlights for price list, reviews and how to order. Now a visitor can order without asking a single question.

say: An algorithm is the set of rules an app uses to decide who sees each post. It predicts what each person will watch, comment on, save or share.
Halima sells zobo in Kaduna. Her flyer with prices reached about 120 accounts, with only 2 saves.

cards.d: Reached about 400 accounts, with 35 saves. Useful posts get saved.
Reached about 1,900 accounts, mostly non-followers, with 14 shares.

say: Her carousel, five ways to serve zobo at a party, reached about 400 accounts and was saved 35 times, because it was useful.

cards.d: Reached about 400 accounts, with 35 saves. Useful posts get saved.
Reached about 1,900 accounts, mostly non-followers, with 14 shares.

say: Her short Reel of chilled zobo poured over ice reached about 1,900 accounts, mostly non-followers.
So she now posts one useful carousel and two Reels a week, and keeps prices in a pinned post. Her own Insights beat any general rule.

say: Turn on two-factor authentication everywhere. Takeovers of Nigerian business pages often start with a fake support message, so never share a login code, even for a verified badge.
Never buy followers. They do not buy from you, and they can reduce your reach. And always ask before posting a customer's photo, name or chat, with phone numbers blurred.

panel.heading: Protect your accounts and customers
items: Two-factor authentication on every account
Never share login codes with 'Meta support'
Never buy followers or likes
Ask before posting a customer's photo or chat

say: To remember. Write your customer sentence first. Use one main platform, one support, and WhatsApp to close. Your bio says what, where, proof and how to order. Useful posts get saved and short Reels travel. And track enquiries, not just followers.
